blocks.content: An Ombudsman is an officer appointed by the legislature to supervise the administration, investigate complaints against administrative officialdom, and report findings back to the legislature.

rows: President (on recommendation of a Selection Committee)
Covers executive, judiciary, and military personnel
Covers PM, Ministers, MPs, Group A-D officers (Judiciary excluded)
Can take Suo-Motu action and act on complaints
Acts on complaints received; limited suo-motu powers

items: Sweden was the world's first country to constitutionalize the Ombudsman system in 1809.
The First Administrative Reforms Commission (1966) headed by Morarji Desai recommended the setting up of Lokpal and Lokayukta in India.
New Zealand (1962) was the first Commonwealth country to adopt the Ombudsman institution under the Parliamentary Commissioner Act.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The institution of Ombudsman was first established in Sweden in 1809 to protect citizens from administrative injustice and corruption.
Etymologically, 'Ombudsman' is a Swedish word meaning an officer, representative, or delegate acting on behalf of citizens.
The Scandinavian Ombudsman model functions as an independent officer appointed by the legislature to supervise executive administration.
In India, the concept of Ombudsman was institutionalized as Lokpal at the Central level and Lokayuktas at the State level based on ARC recommendations.
The Ombudsman generally possesses powers of investigation, inquiry, and recommendation, operating free from executive interference.
